summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her ninth cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well, with expected mild transaminitis and manageable nausea and arthralgias. Methotrexate levels cleared appropriately by day three, allowing for safe discharge. An MRI during admission showed a slight decrease in the size of the right frontal lobe lesion and reduced enhancement, indicating a positive treatment response. She remained neurologically stable, with chronic right foot pain managed on gabapentin. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to restart mesalamine, continue enoxaparin, and follow up with oncology in two weeks for her next cycle.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
